First, let's recall the graph of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13942972/assets/fbf6ef1ca91f998ab4dc2dda1890ffc8a713f2eeff19e5569351b2466256d63a.png)

From the graph, we note the following:

- The period of $\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ is $2\pi .$

- Our graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis. This means that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ is an *even* function, and we have

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(-x)=\operatorname{sec}⁡x.
$$

Let's now evaluate our expression:

- Firstly, using the periodicity of $\operatorname{sec}⁡x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡(-a+20\pi ) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(-a+2\pi \cdot 10) \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(-a).\end{aligned}
$$

- Secondly, using the evenness of $\operatorname{sec}⁡x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡(-a) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡a \\  & =\sqrt{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\operatorname{sec}⁡(-a+20\pi )=\sqrt{7}.$
